"""
Advanced LRU Cache with Time-To-Live (TTL) Expiry and Thread Safety.

This module provides a high-performance, thread-safe Least Recently Used (LRU) cache
implementation that supports configurable Time-To-Live (TTL) expiration for cached entries.
It is designed for production environments where concurrent access, memory management,
and automatic cleanup of stale data are critical requirements.

Features:
    - O(1) get and put operations using a doubly-linked list and hash map.
    - Configurable maximum size (capacity) to bound memory usage.
    - Per-item or global Time-To-Live (TTL) expiration.
    - Thread-safe operations via fine-grained locking or a single lock, depending on configuration.
    - Callback support for eviction and expiration events.
    - Comprehensive statistics tracking (hits, misses, evictions, expirations).
    - Clean integration with the Python standard library and pytest for testing.

Design Decisions:
    - The core data structure combines a dictionary for O(1) lookups with a doubly-linked
      list to maintain access order. This is a standard but highly efficient pattern.
    - TTL expiration is handled lazily on access and eagerly during eviction.
      A background thread is NOT used to avoid complexity and overhead; instead,
      expired items are removed when they are accessed or when the cache needs to
      evict an item due to capacity constraints.
    - Thread safety is achieved using a threading.RLock to allow re-entrant locking
      for internal helper methods.
